method: ENTIRELY from AMH across three pages, read under subscription and PARAPHRASED: no passage reproduced, no source_text stored, every claim carries its page's locator and the verdict licensed_source_not_quoted, so NOTHING here is machine re-checkable. A targeted search of RACGP's open AJGP for poisoning, overdose or activated charcoal returned NO results at all; that absence is recorded rather than filled. This guideline is written as a general-practice and pre-hospital decision document -- when decontamination is and is not indicated, and who to ring -- not as an emergency department protocol. AMH itself directs the reader to a Poisons Information Centre on 13 11 26 twice, and that instruction is carried prominently.

claims.claim: Gastrointestinal decontamination involves the use of activated charcoal and/or whole bowel irrigation to reduce systemic absorption of an ingested poison; GASTRIC LAVAGE IS INFREQUENTLY USED AND INDUCTION OF EMESIS, FOR EXAMPLE WITH IPECACUANHA, IS NO LONGER ADVISED
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Gastrointestinal decontamination' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/antidotes-antivenoms/gastrointestinal-decontaminants/gastrointestinal-decontamination, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22
